title: Binding-affinity prediction: experimental noise floor, attenuation ceiling, and whole-target holdout on ChEMBL Ki
converted_by: tracks/suite/make-cases.mjs; numbers are the agent's own, times are file times, see the header of that script

statement.text: The law under test is the attenuation bound: for any predictor whose errors are uncorrelated with assay noise, Pearson r against a single noisy measurement satisfies r <= sqrt(vy/(vy+s^2)), where s is the SD of one measurement; and a predictor that knows only the target attains r^2 = the between-target share of variance. Both are stated and proved in the checked Lean file <home>/.antigravity-ide/ScienceClaw/delphisci/tracks/research/lean/q2-theory-lean__Q2Theory.lean as Q2.pearson_attenuation (with Q2.attenuation_tight for attainment) and Q2.r2_target_only / Q2.target_only_floor

lean.reason: No Lean file was written for this case in the run; the law is checked against data only.

holdout.holdout_set: Whole TARGETS held out by an untunable rule: a target is held out iff int(sha256(target_chembl_id),16) mod 4 == 0. performance.verdict_basis: On targets it has not seen the model is worse than a constant in RMSE and below the target-mean baseline. The same model scores r 0.824 on a random split, which is the leak the case set out to show.

baseline.name: leave-one-out target mean (knows the target, not the compound), r

broken_input_control.description: training labels shuffled: r fell from 0.164 to 0.004

items.what: In the law: nothing was falsified, but the ceiling is close to useless as a diagnostic. Its own estimate is unstable - 0.882 from squared replicate differences versus 0.977 from the replicate correlation (r = 0.954, n = 2,132) on the SAME held-out data - and the leaky score (0.824) already sits inside that gap, so 'the model is near the noise ceiling' can be true of a purely memorising model. The bound also assumes predictor error is uncorrelated with assay noise, which fails exactly under leaka
